title: Hiring heuristics & interview case curation guide
content:
Purpose

This note collects a compact set of heuristics, an interview rubric template, and a small curated case bank to standardize time-to-decision while improving candidate experience for engineering and product hires. It is intended for People Ops partners, hiring managers, and interviewers who create or pick interview cases.

Scope
- Roles: IC Software Engineer (backend/infra), Applied ML Engineer, Product Engineer, Developer Experience.
- Stages covered: phone screen -> tech loop -> manager loop -> debrief -> offer.
- Not covered: executive leadership hiring, contractor-only triage (separate flow).

High-level hiring heuristics (short form)
- Prioritize signal that maps to day-1 impact: design clarity, debugging process, communication, and small-feedback loop coding.
- Prefer narrower, realistic cases over contrived puzzles. Realistic = reflects the work they will do in first 3 months (e.g., service debugging, inference performance trade-offs, API design for function calling).
- Timebox every case (typically 30–60m). Clearly state inputs/outputs and constraints.
- Always include a one-paragraph context blurb for each case (why it matters to Redwood).
- Interviews should gather at least two distinct signals: technical competence + collaboration/communication.

Interview rubric (single-page template)
Score scale: 1–5 (1 = well below bar; 3 = meets bar; 5 = far above bar)
Categories (score individually, then compute weighted average):
- Technical correctness & depth (weight 0.40): correctness, algorithmic reasoning, systems thinking.
- Problem decomposition & trade-offs (weight 0.25): ability to break down problem, propose alternatives, evaluate cost/latency/complexity trade-offs.
- Communication & collaboration (weight 0.20): clarity of thought, ability to explain decisions, receptiveness to hints.
- Execution & craft (weight 0.10): coding quality, tests, small optimizations.
- Cultural fit / ownership (weight 0.05): signals about curiosity, ownership, and cross-team empathy.

Pass thresholds (example):
- Strong hire: weighted >= 4.2 with no category < 3.0
- Hire: weighted >= 3.5 with max one category 2.5–3.0 and explicit mitigation plan (mentoring or pair week)
- No-hire: weighted < 3.2 or obvious gaps in safety/security or core systems reasoning for infra roles

Debrief notes template (for interviewer to paste into candidate tracker)
- One-line summary (30–50 chars): e.g., "Backend engineer — strong systems thinker, shy on test coverage"
- Strengths (bullet list)
- Risks / concerns (bullet list and mitigation ideas)
- Score by category: Technical X, Decomp X, Communication X, Execution X, Cultural X
- Recommend: hire / hire-with-plan / no-hire + brief rationale

Case library (curated, short, realistic)
1) Service degradation triage (30–40m) — infra/back-end
Context: A production inference service shows 95th percentile spikes to 800ms for a subset of requests. Logs show increased retry counts and longer KV cache lookups.
Prompt: Walk me through how you would triage (what metrics/logs/traces), outline a debugging plan, and propose short-term and medium-term mitigations. If you want, sketch an experiment to verify whether prefix-KV cache eviction policy is the cause.
Signal: systems reasoning, telemetry literacy, experiment design, prioritization.

2) Cost/latency tradeoff for batching (45m) — infra/applied ML
Context: We have an LLM-serving path where batching improves throughput but increases tail latency for small interactive sessions.
Prompt: Design a routing and batching policy for mixed interactive and batch workloads. Include metrics to monitor, SLA considerations, and a rollout plan. Bonus: include a fallback when GPU pool saturation occurs.
Signal: knowledge of batching, SLO design, graceful degradation, routing heuristics.

3) Small endpoint design + API compatibility (40m) — product/devx
Context: Customers want a structured-output tool-calling API that supports both strict schemas and experimental optional fields.
Prompt: Propose an API contract (request/response), explain versioning and compatibility strategy, and show sample error handling and migration story for an existing client.
Signal: API ergonomics, backward compatibility, product thinking.

4) Model quality regression triage (45m) — applied ML/product
Context: After a model swap to a new quantized variant, we see a drop in BLEU/ROUGE on an internal regression prompt set and a spike in customer complaints about hallucinations.
Prompt: Outline an evaluation and rollback plan. Which offline metrics would you compute? How do you combine automated checks and human reviews to decide whether to rollback or tune the model?
Signal: eval design, labeling strategy, data triage, deployment rollback policy.

Mock collaboration probe (15m) — all roles
- Give candidate a short design that an interviewer will adopt as "customer feedback" mid-interview; measure how they adapt, ask clarifying Qs, and rebalance trade-offs.

Interviewer guidance (practical)
- Start with a 3–5 minute context brief. Re-iterate constraints explicitly (strict latency target? budget?).
- Use whiteboard or shared doc; keep candidate in control of the keyboard for execution segments where possible.
- If a candidate is stuck, give one structured hint and watch for adaptation. Record whether they incorporated feedback.
- Respect timeboxes. Close the loop with a 3–5 minute recap and allow candidate questions.

Recruiter / candidate experience checklist (pre/post interview)
Before interview:
- Send candidate a single-paragraph case context and a short list of tools allowed (e.g., Google, short terminal), plus a reminder of interview duration and interviewer names.
- Ensure interviewer has candidate resume + role rubric loaded (link to tracker).
After interview (within 48h ideally):
- Interviewers submit debrief template. Recruiter synthesizes notes and updates candidate within agreed SLA (48–72h).
- If proceeding to next round, share expected timeline and owner. If not proceeding, provide a short rationale and two concrete improvement pointers (when possible).

Offer and first-week activation checklist (owner assignments)
- People Ops: confirm compensation packet, benefits enrollment link, remote hardware options (3 business days).
- Manager: schedule 30/60/90 expectations meeting, assign buddy, create first-week 50% time for team onboarding + 50% for practical task.
- IT/Infra: provision VPN, repo access, cloud IAM roles, test GPUs (if infra/ml role).
- Buddy: schedule shadow sessions for first 5 days, prepare a small non-critical issue for live pairing on day 3.

Quick templates (copy/paste)
Subject (to candidate): "Interview context — [Role] at Redwood Inference (30m)"
Body: "We look forward to meeting you. The interview will focus on a short realistic case in [systems/API/modeling]. You'll have 30–45 minutes; we will provide context and constraints ahead of time. Please bring a laptop and be prepared to share code or a design doc. No preparation required beyond reviewing your past projects.

Debrief quick score (for fast loops)
- Technical (1–5): 
- Decomp (1–5): 
- Communication (1–5): 
- Execution (1–5): 
- Culture (1–5): 
- Recommendation: hire / hire-with-plan / no-hire

Notes, open questions and next steps
- Maintain a small centralized case bank (this doc is the working index). Cases should be refreshed quarterly; contributors can add PRs to the public repo linked above.
- Experiment: trial a strict 48h interviewer-debrief SLA for fast-moving candidate pipelines and measure impact on offer acceptance.

Appendix: quick interviewer dos/don’ts
Do: share explicit success criteria, be curious about tradeoffs, record concrete examples.
Don't: rely solely on puzzles, ask for memorized trivia, or end interviews >10m without a recap.

-- end of guide --
